newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says to float baht with immediate effect.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says to float baht with immediate effect.

text.p: Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday that the value of the baht would be set by market forces effective July 2.

"The Thai exchange rate system from July 2, 1997 will be a managed float whereby the value of the baht will be determined by market forces to reflect fundamental economic forces," the minister said in a statement.
The baht has been fixed on a daily basis against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.

"Under the new system movements in the exchange rate are expected to be quite large at the initial stage. However, relative stability should be attained after a brief adjustment period," the minister's statement said.
"The Bank of Thailand will intervene in the foreign exchange market from time to time to achieve policy objectives and guard against excessive baht fluctuations."

The announcement that the beleagured baht would be floated confirmed widespread belief in the foreign exchange market that some changes were imminent in the currency after an attack by speculators in May. The baht sank nearly three baht against the U.S. dollar in immediate reaction. In offshore markets it was quoted at 27.000/28.000 compared with around 24.25 just before the news.
